Practices.Summary: MoonshotAI maintains three internal benchmark suites: Kimi Code Bench (end-to-end long-horizon coding tasks), Kimi Design Bench (four categories: Visual Input Tasks, Landing Page Construction, Full-Stack Application Development, General Creative Programming), and Claw Bench (five domains: Coding Tasks, IM Ecosystem Integration, Information Research and Analysis, Scheduled Task Management, Memory Utilization). Each K2.x model release is benchmarked across all three suites.

evidence.quote: On Kimi Code Bench, our internal coding benchmark covering diverse complicated end-to-end tasks, Kimi K2.6 demonstrates significant improvements over Kimi K2.5.
We established an internal Kimi Design Bench, organized into four categories: Visual Input Tasks, Landing Page Construction, Full-Stack Application Development, and General Creative Programming.

Performance gains are quantified by our internal Claw Bench, the evaluation suite spanning five domains: Coding Tasks, IM Ecosystem Integration, Information Research & Analysis, Scheduled Task Management, and Memory Utilization.

Practices.Summary: For external coding benchmarks (SWE-Bench Verified 80.2%, SWE-Bench Pro 58.6%, SWE-Bench Multilingual 76.7%, Terminal-Bench 2.0 66.7%, OSWorld-Verified 73.1%), MoonshotAI uses an in-house evaluation framework adapted from SWE-agent with a minimal tool set (bash, createfile, insert, view, strreplace, submit). Issues.Issue title: Window switching causes focus event information to be printed in kimi cli input
Issues.description: A terminal event-handling bug where switching windows causes focus event escape codes to be injected into the CLI input buffer, corrupting user input.

Issues.Issue title: The kimi cli installed using uv on Windows 11 Enterprise Edition starts too slowly
Issues.description: A startup performance regression on Windows 11 Enterprise where the uv-installed CLI binary shows abnormally long cold-start times compared to other installation methods.
A bug/enhancement reporting that sub-agent execution timeouts are too restrictive for complex long-horizon agentic tasks, causing premature termination during multi-step workflows.

Issues.Issue title: MCP tool list is too long, causing initialization error
Issues.description: A bug where connecting too many MCP tool servers exceeds an internal limit, causing the CLI to fail during initialization and preventing all tool usage from starting.

Issues.Issue title: Session persistence lacks fsync, and there is a risk of data loss when exiting abnormally
Issues.description: A data-integrity issue where session state is written without calling fsync, meaning abnormal termination (crash or kill signal) can corrupt or lose the serialized session data.

Issues.Issue title: Session becomes extremely slow in v1.37.0 after extensive MATLAB work
Issues.description: A version-specific performance regression in v1.37.0 where sessions with large MATLAB computation histories degrade severely in responsiveness, suggesting a context accumulation or serialization bottleneck.

Issues.Issue title: The first line of text has one more character indentation than the other lines
Issues.description: A text rendering bug where the first line of multi-line terminal output is indented by one extra character compared to subsequent lines, causing visual misalignment in the TUI.

Issues.Issue title: Text rendering breaks at line wrap boundaries on Linux terminals (scrollbar-related)
Issues.description: A terminal rendering regression on Linux where text display corrupts at line-wrap boundaries, suspected to be caused by scrollbar interaction with the TUI rendering layer.

Issues.Issue title: [Critical] K2.6 model overloaded - unusable under normal load
Issues.description: A critical availability bug where the K2.6 model backend becomes overloaded under normal user load, causing the CLI to be entirely unusable. Received 4 community comments and was flagged as critical.

Issues.Issue title: [Bug] v1.39.0 /web mode JavaScript file MIME type error causes page to fail loading
Issues.description: A web UI regression in v1.39.0 where JavaScript files are served with an incorrect MIME type, causing the browser to refuse loading the page and rendering /web mode entirely unusable.

Issues.Issue title: Yolo mode incorrectly conflates auto-approve with non-interactive, blocking AskUserQuestion
Issues.description: An agent interaction bug where yolo (auto-approve all) mode is incorrectly treated as non-interactive mode, preventing the AskUserQuestion tool from prompting the user for necessary clarification during agentic tasks.

Issues.Issue title: MCP Server Connection Always Fails on Windows Due to Unicode Encoding Bug in kimi.exe (PyInstaller Python 3.14)
Issues.description: A Windows-specific encoding bug in the PyInstaller-packaged kimi.exe binary under Python 3.14 where Unicode encoding failures prevent MCP server connections from being established at all.

Issues.Issue title: Error code: 400 thinking is enabled but reasoning_content is missing in assistant tool call message
Issues.description: An API compatibility bug where enabling thinking mode while using tool calls produces a 400 error because the API expects reasoning_content in the assistant message but the tool call path omits it.

Issues.Issue title: VS code plugin Plan Mode ExitPlanMode cannot be called
Issues.description: A VS Code extension bug where the ExitPlanMode command is broken in the kimi-agent-sdk VS Code plugin Plan Mode feature, preventing users from programmatically exiting plan mode.

Issues.Issue title: Long history causes high Renderer CPU, suspected lack of virtual scrolling
Issues.description: A web UI performance issue where sessions with long conversation histories cause the renderer to consume high CPU, with the suspected root cause being absence of virtual scrolling for large message lists.

Practices.Summary: MoonshotAI's primary architectural methodology for complex tasks is horizontal scaling via Agent Swarm: the system dynamically decomposes tasks into heterogeneous subtasks executed concurrently by self-created domain-specialized sub-agents. Kimi K2.5 supports 100 sub-agents over 1,500 tool calls; Kimi K2.6 scales to 300 sub-agents over 4,000 coordinated steps, reducing latency by 4.5x over single-agent baselines.

evidence.quote: The architecture scales horizontally to 300 sub-agents executing across 4,000 coordinated steps simultaneously, a substantial expansion from K2.5's 100 sub-agents and 1,500 steps.
Deliver better results 4.5x faster than sequential execution

Practices.Summary: MoonshotAI practices systematic dogfooding as a software engineering methodology. The marketing team uses Claw Groups (Agent Swarm research preview) to run end-to-end content production campaigns. The RL infra team uses K2.6-backed agents for 24/7 autonomous operations, feeding real-world reliability data back into model and product development.

Practices.Summary: Agent Swarm was driven by bottom-up internal engineering practice: an internal team member building a Python cascade of if-else statements for multi-agent stock research recognized at line 100 that she was hand-coding a multi-agent system, which led directly to the formalization of Agent Swarm as a product feature.

evidence.quote: She wrote a Python workflow, a cascade of if-else statements. At line one hundred, she stopped. 'I'm hand-coding a multi-agent system.'

Practices.Summary: The underlying Kimi K2.5/K2.6 model is configured with interleaved thinking and multi-step tool calls as native features. For benchmarks, all K2.6 experiments use temperature = 1.0, top_p = 1.0, and context length of 262,144 tokens. Two inference modes are supported: thinking mode (temperature 1.0) and instant mode (temperature 0.6).

evidence.quote: Unless otherwise specified, all Kimi K2.6 experiments were conducted with temperature = 1.0, top-p = 1.0, and a context length of 262,144 tokens.

Practices.Summary: Context management is a first-class engineering concern in the prompt pipeline: when the context window exceeds the threshold, only the most recent round of tool-related messages is retained (discard strategy). This prevents context window overflow during long-horizon tasks with thousands of tool calls without requiring full history compression.
